title: Two-Pass Camera Raw Workflow with Pattern-Driven Cropping and Directional Lighting in Fall-Loli Landscape

date.basis: embedded_creation_time metadata; approximate creation date; transcript does not independently confirm actual shooting date

summary: This video segment presents a concise landscape post-processing workflow focused on fall-color scenes. The presenter emphasizes pattern-based cropping to isolate repeating dark-light or color patterns, introduces a directional lighting cue (visually simulated with editing), and demonstrates a two-pass RAW workflow in Photoshop using Camera Raw. The sequence covers expanding dynamic range by adjusting shadows and blacks, performing global saturation tweaks, color-balancing toward blues, and using curves and color calibration to enhance river and foliage details. The narration also notes ISO exposure considerations during capture, references Icelandic-style landscapes as contextual examples, and clarifies that the discussion centers on post-processing technique rather than confirming a filming location.

sections.title: Pattern-driven composition and initial lighting adjustments
sections.description: Introduces the goal of cropping to isolate a repeating color/pattern motif, discusses subtle directional lighting to guide the viewer's eye, and demonstrates a quick dodge/ burn approach to illustrate the light direction and its impact on overall composition.

featured_techniques.technique: Cropping to isolate a repeating pattern (dark/light or color alternation) to guide viewer attention
Simulated directional lighting using quick dodge/ burn to steer the eye
Global tonal adjustment and color balancing (lower exposure, increase overall saturation, then bias toward blues)
Curve-based enhancement to bring out river and color detail
Two-pass Camera Raw workflow in Photoshop (Camera Raw filter, then re-open RAW for a second pass)
